filename: Discovering Causal Relations and Equations from Data_.pdf
title: Discovering causal relations and equations from data
research_field: Climate and Physical Sciences / Machine Learning
processes: Ocean mesoscale turbulence and eddy-mean flow interactions
Boundary-layer transition to turbulence and wall-bounded flows
ml_methods: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems (SINDy)
parameterization_target: Ocean mesoscale eddy closures (subgrid-scale momentum and potential vorticity forcing)
host_model: Idealized ocean primitive equation / quasi-geostrophic model
code_availability: Software packages reviewed include Tigramite, causal-learn, Tetrad, pcalg, bnlearn, PyWhy, seqICP, rEDM, PySR, gplearn, Glyph, and Operon. Benchmark platform referenced at https://causeme.net.
testbed_rationale: This paper is a comprehensive review article summarizing methods, frameworks, and case studies across physics, Earth sciences, and neuroscience rather than presenting a single newly released benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Observational data limitations: theoretical impossibility of proving causal graphs purely from observational data without untestable assumptions (e.g., faithfulness, causal sufficiency)
Nonstationarity, autocorrelations, and multiscale temporal dynamics causing inflated false discovery rates in time series causal inference
High dimensionality of spatiotemporal fields requiring aggressive dimensionality reduction prior to discovery
Curse of dimensionality in candidate library construction for sparse regression and symbolic regression
Generalization failures of black-box neural network parameterizations under out-of-distribution regime shifts (e.g., from isotropic eddies to anisotropic jet regimes)
extraction_notes: The paper is a major review in Physics Reports co-authored by LEAP and ERC-funded researchers covering causal discovery and symbolic/implicit equation discovery across climate, fluid mechanics, and neuroscience.
